slides.title: Three promises
slides.text: Security work protects three promises about information. It stays secret, it stays correct, and it stays reachable when its owner needs it. Professionals shorten that to confidentiality, integrity and availability.
slides.alt: A later protocol level on the road: here a damaged packet must be spotted by its count and sent again.

focus.cue: Correct: every packet carries a dot count
A match at the far end means it is whole

slides.title: A read letter
slides.text: Confidentiality breaks first in our story: a sealed letter is steamed open and read on its journey. The words arrive unchanged, but the secret is gone, and the promise with it.
slides.alt: Lock 2 at Pro: the Magpie's sealed note waits beside the cipher wheel. No first letter is given this time.

focus.cue: A sealed note keeps its words secret

slides.title: A changed address
slides.text: Integrity breaks differently: the letter is never read, but its address is altered, so the package goes to the wrong house. Availability breaks loudest of all: the sorting office itself burns down.
slides.alt: Lock 1 at Pro: the golden letter must cross Netville to the sorting room, and the short road is not always open.

focus.cue: Change the route, and it reaches the wrong door

slides.title: Rules stack too
slides.text: Society stacks its own layers: house rules, your school's acceptable use policy, the app's terms, then copyright and privacy law. Each layer is enforced by different people, with different tools.
slides.alt: Would you rather use a nickname nobody can trace to you, or your real first name so friends can find you?

focus.cue: An app's rules decide what may be posted
And the law protects what is yours

slides.title: Which promise broke?
slides.text: Three failures reached Pim this week. Name the promise each one broke.
steps: A private photo shown to strangers: confidentiality
A delivery note edited in transit: integrity
The whole message service down all day: availability
slides.alt: The whole journey of a picture in five rule cards, waiting to be put in the right order.

focus.cue: The five rule cards for the whole journey
Put them in the order they happen

slides.title: Agreements protect users too
slides.text: Agreements are not only the owner's shield. Terms also promise users things: notice before changes, a way to appeal, a route to complain. When rules are broken against you, the rulebook names who must act.
slides.alt: Would you rather use a picture someone else made and credit them, or draw your own from scratch?

focus.cue: Use someone's picture: the rules protect its maker
Or make your own: your work is protected too

words.means: information stays secret from everyone but its audience
information and services stay reachable when needed
the terms both sides accept, which can protect users too

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Would You Rather at Online: share or keep. For each dilemma, name which of the three promises is at stake.
slides.alt: Would you rather ask a trusted adult before every download, or never download anything at all?

focus.cue: Play Online: which promise is at stake?
